html:
SMTO-EXE-0016 — SMTO didn't recognize that recovery choice

GUID: 4b769f9b-6961-4019-92ad-2300d4ad9553
Slug: resource-reconciliation-invalid-action
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • The choice sent to deal with a blocking job isn't one the Gateway accepts, so nothing was done. Your blocked command still hasn't started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page so the recovery card in the task shows the current choices. Reloading picks up the choices SMTO currently offers, in case SMTO or the page was recently updated.
  2. On the card, select Wait until the job state changes or Resolve forcefully by terminating job. These are the only two choices SMTO offers for a blocking job, and SMTO turns them into requests the Gateway accepts.

What success looks like

  • The card shows Waiting for the job state to change… or Blocking job claims restored.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO and its Gateways; SMTO and the Gateway may be on mismatched versions. Don't keep resending the same choice; it will be refused again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's blocker-control commit (GatewayJobs.control_blockers) rejected the request because its action was neither stop nor override.

What this means

  • The Gateway's blocker-control endpoint received an action other than its supported stop or override choices. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The Gateway's blocker-control endpoint received an action other than its supported stop or override choices.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the submitted action with the current control endpoint's supported choices; reset and baseline acceptance use their own flows.

How to fix it

  • The Gateway job-control endpoint maps only stop_resource_blockers and authorize_resource_override to stop/override, so this points to an internal caller passing another action or a Server/Gateway version mismatch. Find that caller, bring the Server and Gateway to matching versions, then refresh the run's recovery state and submit a supported action.
  • Refresh the current recovery choices and select a supported action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The existing UI or client submits a supported action to its owning endpoint.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
